message.content: {"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS000753","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All 6 candidates are direct matches on trait/efo and have endpoint-faithful phenotyping (abdominal aortic aneurysm; one is explicitly prevalent AAA). Two candidates come from generic framework papers (PGS001784: “Global Biobank analyses…”; PGS002054: “Portability of 245 polygenic scores…”), which domain guidance down-ranks when disease-focused alternatives exist. Among the remaining disease-focused options, PGS000753 (MVP/Mayo-VDB; Circulation AAA genetics) provides the cleanest PRS-specific signal in the visible metadata via an effect size (OR per SD 1.37, 95% CI 1.30–1.44) with basic covariates (age, sex, PCs) and a reasonably sized validation (n=46,564). Competing newer disease-focused scores (PGS003972/PGS003973 Nat Genet; PGS003429 Nat Commun) report only full-model discrimination metrics (AUROC/C-index) with unknown/varied covariate disclosure, and no PGS-only/incremental metrics are shown here, making cross-candidate performance comparison ambiguous per the provided policy; additionally, the very high C-index in PGS003973 cannot be interpreted as PRS-driven without PRS-only or incremental reporting. Main limitation: absence of PRS-only AUROC/R2 for PGS000753 and non-comparable/insufficiently specified performance reporting across the other disease-focused candidates prevents a clearly high-confidence best choice."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_HIGH_QUALITY","best_model_id":"PGS003972","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All 6 candidates are direct matches (trait_reported/trait_efo and phenotyping_reported align to abdominal aortic aneurysm or prevalent AAA). Several are framework/portability-style scores (PGS001784: Global Biobank lessons; PGS002054: UKB portability of 245 scores), which domain_knowledge advises down-ranking when disease-focused alternatives exist unless they have clearly superior endpoint/metric evidence. Among disease-focused options, PGS003972 and PGS003973 come from a dedicated AAA GWAS meta-analysis (Nat Genet 2023) with multi-cohort development and European evaluation; PGS003972 additionally has broader development cohort support listed (includes UKB and VIVA, which are not listed for PGS003973), while both use PRS-CS with dense variant sets. Reported discrimination is not directly comparable across all models (many only show full-model AUROC/C-index and several have missing PRS-only metrics); PGS003973’s higher C-index (0.882) may be largely covariate-driven and cannot be treated as PGS-only, and the heritability note cautions against over-interpreting high full-model AUROC/C-index without PRS-isolated metrics. Given comparable endpoint fidelity, stronger disease-focused study context versus framework scores, and slightly stronger development/validation evidence package visibility for PGS003972, it is the best-supported choice, but confidence is limited by missing PRS-only/incremental metrics and non-comparable performance reporting across candidates."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS000753","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All 6 candidates are direct matches by trait/efo and have acceptable endpoint alignment (phenotyping_reported is AAA diagnosis; one is explicitly prevalent but still aligned). However, comparable PRS-only performance is largely missing: several models report only full-model AUROC/C-index (likely covariate-influenced) and/or non-AUC metrics (partial-r), limiting clean cross-model ranking. Among disease-focused candidates, PGS000753 (Circulation; MVP/Mayo-VDB; P+T, 29 variants) provides a clear PRS effect size (OR per SD 1.37, 95% CI 1.30–1.44) with basic covariates and moderate validation size (n=46,564), making it the most interpretable PRS-specific signal in the provided metadata. Competing framework-style scores include PGS001784 (Global Biobank analyses; PRS-CS-auto) and PGS002054 (UKB portability), which are down-weighted by their pan-trait/portability context despite large validation or reported PRS-only R2; and PGS003973 shows a very high C-index (0.882) but only as a full-model metric with age/sex covariates and no isolated PRS-only metric, so its apparent advantage is not directly comparable. Because the evidence base is heterogeneous and PRS-only discrimination is not consistently reported across candidates, the recommendation remains sub-optimal rather than high-confidence."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS000753","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All 6 candidates are direct matches (trait_reported/trait_efo and phenotyping_reported all indicate abdominal aortic aneurysm, with one explicitly prevalent AAA). Several models come from pan-trait/framework contexts (PGS001784: global biobank lessons; PGS002054: UKB portability), which domain guidance says should generally not outrank a disease-focused candidate unless they have clearly cleaner endpoint and PRS-comparable performance evidence. Among the disease-focused options, PGS000753 (MVP/Mayo-VDB AAA study) has clear endpoint fidelity (prevalent AAA), basic covariates (age/sex/PCs), and provides a PRS effect size (OR per SD 1.37, 95% CI 1.30–1.44), offering PRS-specific signal without relying on full-model AUROC. Competing disease-focused Nat Genet models (PGS003972/PGS003973) report only full-model discrimination (AUROC/C-index) with basic covariates but lack PRS-only metrics/effect sizes in the provided metadata, and one shows a very high C-index (0.882) that is likely dominated by age/sex given AAA’s low heritability, making cross-model PRS contribution comparison uncertain. Because most candidates lack directly comparable PRS-only AUROC/R2 and key covariate/endpoint details are missing for some (e.g., ‘Unknown’ covariates), selection is supported but not definitive, hence sub-optimal with moderate confidence."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS003972","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All 6 candidates are direct matches on trait_reported/trait_efo and use an AAA diagnosis endpoint, but the evidence does not cleanly identify a single best PRS because most reported discrimination metrics are full-model and covariates are sometimes unknown. PGS003972 (Nat Genet 2023 AAA GWAS meta-analysis; PRS-CS; large multi-cohort development including multiple AAA-relevant cohorts) is best supported by disease-focused, multi-cohort context and direct endpoint alignment; its reported AUROC=0.69 is modest and not clearly PRS-only, but it avoids the strongest framework/portability penalties compared with PGS001784 (global biobank framework) and PGS002054 (UKB portability paper). PGS003973 reports a higher C-index (0.882) but this appears to be a full model with age/age^2/sex and is not PRS-comparable; without PRS-only metrics or incremental performance, it is uncertain whether it truly outperforms PGS003972 on genetic contribution. Overall, direct-match candidates exist, but missing PRS-only metrics/incremental AUROC and mixed reporting prevent a high-confidence best-choice call."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS003972","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All 6 candidates are direct matches on trait/efo and use abdominal aortic aneurysm endpoints, so selection hinges on study archetype and comparability of performance evidence. PGS003972 (Nat Genet AAA GWAS meta-analysis; PRS-CS; multi-cohort development spanning many AAA studies/biobanks; EUR evaluation) is the most clearly disease-focused, multi-cohort score in this set, aligning with the domain-knowledge preference for cardiovascular/large-vessel disease-focused meta-analyses over portability/framework scores. Competing models include: (i) PGS001784 (Cell Genomics ‘Global Biobank analyses…’) and PGS002054 (‘Portability of 245 polygenic scores…’) which are explicitly framework/portability papers and should be down-ranked absent clearly superior PRS-isolated metrics; (ii) PGS003429 (Nat Commun screening cost-effectiveness) which is less clearly a pure PRS evaluation and has unknown covariates; (iii) PGS000753 is older and very sparse (29 variants) though it reports an OR=1.37. Limitation: available discrimination metrics are not PRS-isolated for most candidates (often only full-model AUROC/C-index, and covariate sets differ/are sometimes unknown). In particular, PGS003973 reports a high full-model C-index (0.882) but with only age/age^2/sex covariates and without PRS-only metrics, making it hard to compare PRS contribution; this prevents a high-confidence ‘best’ choice, so the outcome is sub-optimal despite a preferred disease-focused study context."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_HIGH_QUALITY","best_model_id":"PGS003972","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All 6 candidates are direct matches on trait/efo and have aligned diagnosis-style phenotyping_reported (AAA; one is explicitly prevalent AAA). Two candidates (PGS003972, PGS003973) come from a dedicated AAA GWAS meta-analysis (Nat Genet, 2023) with large, disease-focused multi-cohort development, which domain guidance prefers over pan-trait/portability frameworks when endpoint fidelity is comparable. Between these two, PGS003972 is preferred because its development cohorts list is broader (includes UKB and VIVA in addition to multiple external cohorts) and it represents a coherent disease-focused, multi-cohort evidence package; both report only full-model discrimination (AUROC/C-index) with limited PRS-only isolation, so the very high C-index for PGS003973 cannot be treated as clear PRS superiority, especially since it uses age/sex covariates and no PRS-only R2/AUROC is provided. Remaining limitation: key performance evidence is not directly comparable across candidates (mostly full-model AUROC/C-index; PRS-only metrics largely missing), and covariates are unknown for PGS003972, so confidence is moderate rather than high."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS000753","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All 6 candidates are direct matches by trait/efo and have aligned phenotyping (abdominal aortic aneurysm), but the evidence is mixed and often not PRS-comparable (several report only full-model AUROC/C-index or partial-r, with many key PRS-only metrics missing). PGS000753 is preferred because it comes from a disease-focused AAA genetics study (Million Veteran Program; Circulation) with a clearly stated endpoint ('Prevalent abdominal aortic aneurysm'), basic covariates (age/sex/PCs), multi-ancestry evaluation reported, and an interpretable effect size (OR per SD 1.37, 95% CI 1.30–1.44) rather than relying on potentially covariate-driven full-model discrimination. Competing models have limitations: PGS001784 and PGS002054 originate from broad framework/portability papers (Cell Genomics global biobank PRS; UKB portability study) and/or emphasize modest PRS-only/partial-r metrics; PGS003429 and PGS003972 provide only full-model AUROC with unknown covariates; PGS003973 reports a high C-index but this appears to be a full-model metric with demographic covariates and is not directly comparable to PRS-only performance. Because no candidate provides clean, directly comparable PRS-only discrimination evidence across models, the selection remains sub-optimal with moderate confidence."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS000753","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All 6 candidates are direct matches on trait_reported/trait_efo and have phenotype labels consistent with abdominal aortic aneurysm, but the evidence package is mixed and performance reporting is not consistently PRS-comparable. PGS000753 is preferred because it comes from a disease-focused abdominal aortic aneurysm genetics study (Million Veteran Program; Circulation) with an explicitly aligned endpoint (prevalent abdominal aortic aneurysm), basic covariate adjustment (age, sex, PCs), and a reported per-SD effect size (OR=1.37, 95% CI 1.30–1.44), providing PRS-specific signal even though AUROC/R2 are not provided. Competing models either appear to come from broad framework/portability efforts (PGS001784 from a global biobank lessons framework; PGS002054 from a UKB portability paper) where reported metrics (e.g., partial-r=0.0144 or full-model AUROC=0.868 with very small covariates-regressed-out R2=0.014661) may not translate into clearly superior standalone PRS evidence, or report only full-model discrimination with unknown covariates (PGS003429/PGS003972) which limits comparability. Remaining limitation: the most recent disease-meta-analysis family scores (PGS003972/PGS003973) show higher full-model metrics but lack PRS-only/incremental reporting here, and PGS000753 lacks AUROC/R2, so the best choice is not definitively separated; hence DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL with moderate confidence."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS000753","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All 6 candidates are direct matches on trait/EFO and have endpoint-faithful phenotyping (abdominal aortic aneurysm; one is explicitly prevalent AAA). Several candidates come from pan-trait/framework contexts (PGS001784: “Global Biobank analyses…”; PGS002054: “Portability of 245 polygenic scores…”), which domain guidance says to down-rank when disease-focused alternatives exist unless they have clearly stronger, PRS-comparable evidence. Among the remaining disease-focused options, PGS000753 (MVP/MAYO-VDB AAA genetics paper) provides clean demographic covariates (age/sex/PCs), explicit effect-size evidence (OR per SD 1.37, 95% CI 1.30–1.44), and substantial validation (n=46,564) without relying on potentially non-comparable full-model AUROC. {"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS004561","confidence":"Low","rationale":"Two direct-match candidates are present (PGS004491, PGS004561), both aligned to acute kidney injury via consistent trait_efo and identical endpoint coding in phenotyping_reported/trait_reported (N17 acute renal failure), from the same 2024 Commun Biol publication, same EUR-only DEV/EVAL ancestry context, same training cohort (UKB) and training/validation sample sizes, and both lack comparable discrimination metrics (AUC/R2 fields are null; covariates are Unknown).
